facts.value: Computes an angular argument using atanf(y/x), sign-bit tests, and pi-based quadrant corrections. If x is either signed zero, it returns pi/2 with the sign of y, including when y is also zero. This implementation therefore has its own zero-axis behavior and should not be assumed to follow every standard atan2 signed-zero special case.

facts.value: Under __MWERKS__, saves the input sign bit and clears it before reduction. Small inputs and reciprocal-reduced large inputs retain lookup_index=-1; subsequent relative offsets 27 and 20 select table entries 26 and 19, both zero. The source forms atanf_lookup-1 before these indexed reads, so this is compiler-specific source rather than a portable-C bounds guarantee. Large inputs reconstruct relative to pi/2; the other path ORs the saved sign into the result.
facts.rationale: Record exact branch behavior and source constraints instead of assuming full standard-library exceptional-value guarantees.

evidence.why: Shows sign handling, branch conditions, and reconstruction.

facts.value: For either signed-zero x, returns positive pi/2 for nonnegative-sign y and negative pi/2 for negative-sign y, including both-zero pairs. For finite nonzero x, uses atanf(y/x) with minus pi when both sign bits are negative and plus pi when x is negative but y is not. No explicit NaN or infinity-pair handling is present.
facts.rationale: Record exact branch behavior and source constraints instead of assuming full standard-library exceptional-value guarantees.
